condition_semantics.direct: readout(clean final residual - clean MLP output + corrupt MLP output), all tensors token 12; downstream components fixed to their clean values
condition_semantics.identity: clean destination, replace node with its clean capture
condition_semantics.node_patch: corrupt destination, paired clean source, MLP output after down projection at token 12
condition_semantics.node_patch_all_late: corrupt destination, paired clean source at each of layers 8,9,10,11 during ordinary forward
condition_semantics.node_reverse: clean destination, paired corrupt source at same node
condition_semantics.restore: clean destination, zero node then replace with its clean capture in callback order
condition_semantics.zero: clean destination, replace selected MLP output at token 12 with zero

fixture_selection: SHA-256 greater-than-v1/{split}/{YY:02d}; years in centuries 11..17 after original tokenization filter; one example per suffix 02..98 per split; independently chosen released noun; no model-output selection

metric_definitions.probabilities: stable F64 softmax over unchanged F32 final-token logits, all 50257 tokens; never renormalize numeric subset
metric_definitions.recovery: (condition PD - corrupt PD)/(clean PD - corrupt PD) only if abs(gap)>1e-6; otherwise null
metric_definitions.variation: per-prompt outcomes, mean and sample standard deviation; held-out primary, development diagnostic

hypotheses: Clean prompts tend to favor later years more than matched 01 corruption.
Preselected late MLP node patches may recover part of the clean-to-corrupt gap.
Direct late-MLP readout contributions affect the greater-than distribution.
scientific_expectations.interpretation: Report every preselected condition and per-prompt variation even if a hypothesis fails; original 10000-sample aggregate and full circuit are not pass criteria.

tolerance_status: Frozen before running this 194-prompt study; informed by GPT-2 two-prompt prerequisite and stable F64 analysis. Any future revision must retain failed measurement and explicitly mark post-observation changes.
